scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: The organiser’s voice
scenes.caption: A voice message resembles the club organiser. It asks Isha to send a voucher for new equipment before lunch. The familiar voice and matching photograph make the request feel personal.
scenes.dialogue: Familiar media can carry an unverified request.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: How media can mislead
scenes.caption: Her teacher explains that recordings may be edited, reused or generated. A genuine old recording can also appear in a misleading context. The class cannot tell which happened here merely by listening, and does not need to establish the production method first.
scenes.dialogue: The requested action still needs checking.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: No magic detection clue
scenes.caption: One pupil suggests looking for strange blinking or robotic sounds. Such clues are unreliable: convincing manipulated media may lack obvious glitches, while genuine recordings can have poor quality. A smooth clip cannot prove identity, authority or permission to transfer value.
scenes.dialogue: Do not turn appearance into a verdict.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: The verification choice
scenes.caption: Isha can send the voucher, judge the voice more carefully, or ask her teacher to contact the organiser through the club’s previously known route. Choose a plan that verifies the request itself before anyone acts on it.
scenes.dialogue: Check the request, not just the clip.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: A different instruction
scenes.caption: The organiser confirms through that route that no voucher was requested. Isha pauses the transfer and preserves a minimal fictional note for the teacher. She does not circulate the clip as entertainment or publicly name someone as the creator without evidence.
scenes.dialogue: A denial changes the action plan.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Now it is live
scenes.caption: The lab introduces a live-looking video call asking for a file instead. Build a new verification plan: higher realism does not remove the need to confirm a consequential request through an independent known channel.
scenes.dialogue: Realistic is not the same as verified.
